report.source_text: The biopsy showed infiltration by sheets of atypical plasmacytoid cells with some multinucleated forms. Skeletal muscle was also seen. There was no lung parenchyma. Immunohistochemical staining demonstrated that this population was positive for CD138 and MUM1 and weakly positive for CD56. TTF1, p63, S100, AE1/AE3, CD3, CD20 and CD79a were negative. Ki67 was remarkably high (90%). Further immunostains performed at King’s College Hospital reference laboratory revealed that CD38 was strongly positive, there was lambda light chain restriction seen on the immunostaining as well as ISH. Cyclin d1, CD45, pancytokeratin and kappa were negative. Epstein-Barr virus encoded small nuclear RNAs was negative.

An intervertebral deposit at level T4/T5 was seen to be causing significant compression of the adjacent thoracic cord.

report.source_text: In light of the results of lung biopsy, myeloma screen and bone marrow aspirate and trephine were carried out. Immunoglobulin studies showed a slightly low IgA level of 0.62 g/L with a normal IgM level. Protein electrophoresis demonstrated the presence of 2 g/L of paraprotein consisting of IgG lambda paraprotein and lambda light chains. Light chain studies showed a normal free kappa concentration of 6.12 mg/L and an elevated free lambda concentration of 1178.1. His kappa/lambda ratio was reduced at 0.01. Bone marrow aspirate, trephine and immunophenotyping showed no evidence of infiltration by myeloma. Routine viral serology was negative for hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV 1/2.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old man presented on 23 January 2019 with a 6-week history of left-sided sharp chest pain (worse with breathing and laying down), progressive back pain, abdominal distention, and lower limb weakness and numbness suggestive of spinal cord compression. Initial chest X-ray revealed a left upper lobe mass raising suspicion for primary lung cancer. Spinal MRI demonstrated widespread skeletal metastatic disease with three large thoracic paraspinal soft-tissue deposits (largest on left at T2/T3) and an intervertebral deposit at T4/T5 causing significant thoracic cord compression. Lung biopsy was performed to evaluate the chest mass and unexpectedly revealed plasmablastic myeloma rather than primary lung malignancy. Pathology showed sheets of atypical plasmacytoid cells with multinucleated forms, with immunohistochemistry demonstrating CD138+, MUM1+, CD56 weakly+, CD38 strongly+, lambda light chain restriction, and markedly elevated Ki67 (90%). Myeloma workup confirmed IgG lambda paraprotein (2 g/L), elevated free lambda (1178.1), and reduced kappa/lambda ratio (0.01), though bone marrow aspirate and trephine showed no myeloma infiltration. CBC and serum chemistry were normal on admission. The patient was treated with radiotherapy to the spine and chemotherapy with bortezomib, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisolone (VCAP), with repeat imaging showing reduction in size of spinal lesions.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Lung biopsy showed plasmacytoid cells with CD138+, MUM1+, CD38+ immunophenotype and was negative for TTF1, p63, AE1/AE3, and other lung-specific markers (E006), confirming extramedullary myeloma rather than primary pulmonary malignancy
